dedupe_keys.name: freshwater watch citizen science freshwater quality dataset earthwatch

description: FreshWater Watch is a citizen science project run by Earthwatch in which volunteers around the world test local rivers, lakes and ponds and upload results. Each survey records nitrate and phosphate levels, turbidity, the presence of algae and other visual factors at a sampling point, and the site derives a good, moderate or poor ecological status from these readings. Results appear on a global map refreshed hourly, filtered charts can be exported as CSV, and the full unfiltered global dataset can be downloaded as XLSX or CSV, refreshed every Monday (last on 21 September 2026); DCAT and RSS catalogue feeds are also offered. The data are described as free and publicly available for anyone, including researchers, governments and policymakers, with no registration, but no formal licence is named and site pages carry an Earthwatch all-rights-reserved notice. Caveats: readings come from simple test kits used by volunteers, so values are ranges, not laboratory measurements, value ranges in filtered CSV exports can turn into dates in spreadsheets, and sampling is uneven in space and time. Simulation uses: screening diffuse pollution and wastewater impacts on receiving waters, filling gaps between official monitoring sites, and validating water quality models in data-poor areas. Related records: the England Catchment Data Explorer (data-england-catchment-data-explorer-river-basin-management).
